description: Add a real configured-agent integration test using ToolCallingLLMStub and the existing provisioned Disk ChannelConfig. Isolate filesystem state in a UUID directory, exercise get/list plus data_source.update_document_permissions through Executor/Factory/Jido and the real Channels -> DataSourceBridge -> DiskBridge -> Storage path, verify persisted direct/inherited ACLs and indexed projection sync, and cover unauthorized mutation denial. No new Action, Disk config, or mock NodeRouter. Validation: repeated focused test, existing Disk agent flow, permission suites, mix q.

comments.text: Execution evidence plan: reuse provisioned provider=disk ChannelConfig; create only a UUID-owned directory; configured ReAct agent via IntegrationAgent and ToolCallingLLMStub; retrieve real folder Record then invoke update_document_permissions via Executor; assert source ACL persistence, inheritance/projection behavior, unrelated state, and unauthorized denial.

Implemented the agent-driven Disk permission integration coverage. The test reuses the provisioned Disk ChannelConfig, creates only a UUID-owned folder tree, uses a configured ReAct agent plus mock OpenAI endpoint, lists the real folder, invokes update_document_permissions through the real service route, and verifies source ACL mutation, child inheritance, indexed projection sync, sibling isolation, and reader denial. Also changed the existing Disk document flow test to reuse the provisioned config. The journey exposed that model-facing compact Record references could not be rebuilt when signed fields were omitted; added authenticated restoration from provenance claims plus contract/security tests. Validation: new integration test passed with seeds 101/202/303; combined Disk integrations 3/3; Record tests 34 + 1 property; mix q passed; diagnostics and diff check clean. Broader DataSourceBridge suite still has 4 pre-existing assumptions that no provisioned Disk config exists and attempts duplicate provider inserts. Ticket remains open because no commit was requested/authorized.

User correction: remove provenance restoration entirely. Keep strict existing provenance verification, define the minimum valid Record fields in Record.zoi_type so real LLM tool schemas advertise them, and make the mock echo that valid minimum from the listed Record. Add only missing schema/minimal-payload coverage; do not duplicate existing tampering tests. Treat serialization changes as contingent on a failing test after the schema correction.

Applied correction: removed all Record restoration/fallback logic from Provenance and Record.from_map. Record.zoi_type now emits an explicit object schema requiring id, kind, parent_id, permissions, attributes, and provenance_ref; tests assert the generated JSON Schema and a valid minimum signed payload while existing tampering tests remain. The mock now echoes those minimum fields from the actual listed Record. Runtime verification showed schema alone does not affect Jido's bounded transport sanitizer: nested permission Records were still depth-summarized. Added a post-validation model-facing RecordResultTransformer (wired after opaque aliasing/media projection) to preserve the required fields and permission semantics without weakening or reconstructing provenance. DiskBridge now represents embedded permissions as canonical Records, and OpaqueAliases recognizes semantic metadata on object schemas. Validation: integration test passed seeds 101/202/303; focused suite 176 tests + 4 properties passed; mix q, diagnostics, and diff check passed. No commit performed.

title: Add agent-driven Disk permission integration test
